data: The variety of the games is incredible, and it keeps it fresh
I think this game is an incredible achievement and well worth the price
The music is incredible, the graphics are charming, and the gameplay is top-notch
Pilot Quest - 10/10 - One of the absolute best games I've ever played
Cherry Difficulty: 2/10 (10/10 if you are my friend)[/b]

Most of the reviews are of the ORIGIONAL version of the game, and not the version that is currently available. Many games have been "fixed" into an infuriating state of tedium. If you look up a guide, it will be obsolete, if you ask advice, you will be ridiculed. After dozens of hours you might find a comment mentioning that "this strat was patched", because you aren't playing the same game the reviews are talking about, this isn't the game the guide was written for. Instead; this is a much grindier, slower, more INTINTIONALLY frustrating game it was apparently always intended to be. Good Luck sucker!

Magic Garden, it was Magic Garden that really clicked with me. I've only played through the first row and finished MG, but the game has me curious for more.

Also shout-out to the Eggplant Show crew, who are doing a book club playthrough over a year and recording podcasts for each game. There are some cool guest artists, too, like Daniel Mullins.

Anyways, this collection of games is super charming and makes me feel like I'm playing on my old gray box NES. And I'm all for experimental stuff, that's why I'm an indie game fanatic. So as a fan, ty UFO50

Absolute banger of a game! Most of the games are super fun albeit challenging and many could even stand well on their own. While it is clear that the majority of the games are callbacks to classics they don't feel stale and offer interesting new takes. The soundtrack is fantastic and worth a purchase on the author's bandcamp for offline listening.

I'm excited to see what the developers come up with in the future!

Litterally 50 peak games in 1, this game deserves goty more than atrobot ever did, Its crazy Please try it, its litteraly 50 great well-made games for so little compared to all the shitty triple A games for 70 dollars.

Be forewarned, every game in this collection is very difficult and requires a lot of learning. I've put a little over 100 hours into this game, and I've cherried 21 of them. I don't have the patience to learn the Intricacies of every game, especially since most of them are decent, but not really refined due to the style (being a glorified flash game) and the fact theres 49 other games that need effort put into them. Sorry, I can't recommend this game.

So difficult they will make you want to staple your scrotum to the ceiling type of hard.

Games that I recommend trying are Cyber Owls, Night Manor, Rakshasa, Valbrace as they have unique mechanics. I'm giving it a thumb down just as a warning for people of how damn hard these games are.

These are the same folks who made Spelunky so I should have known better. I hope your credit score decreases for making an abomination of a game called Vainger. I've never felt so stupid before .

50 "fully fledged games" with "modern design"? All the ones I tried arent even on par with teh NES, C64 and MS libraries.
Overhyped so hard the dissapointment hit me like getting an itchy sweater for Christmas.

good game
insanely fun amount of games. even if you don't like some, there's plenty of them to choose from and plenty of playtime opportunities
I feel transported back to simpler times. With 50 titles, there's something for everyone to enjoy.

This game collection is amazing. Each game is really original and interesting. They really went out of their way to create a very diverse experience and the ufosoft wrapping around it all it just great.

This game somehow accomplishes what every plug n play console has always failed to deliver, which that alone is saying a lot. You might think since it's 50 games in one it's probably not much, just some short games with a bunch of duds, right?

Just look at how many hours I spent on this. Seriously.

So many, and I mean SO many of these games are great experiences on their own. Not knowing any of the games you're about to play is part of the fun too as I had no idea what I was getting into for each one and I was utterly blown away at what some of these games had to offer. It delivers on almost any front or any genre of game you'd expect for that era of consoles and more. It's full of clever designs and heavy amounts of content, a full blown rpg, an open world platformer, point and click adventure, a dungeon crawler, metroidvania - all fully realized games.

There's not much convincing needed to be done past this I'd wager, so if you're interested in the premise of this game then it's a must buy. But fair warning (and my only criticism of the game), a lot of these games are built to be very difficult and sometimes really frustrating, so make sure to pace yourself out with games that are less punishing because otherwise you're going to get very easily fatigued. Make sure to play Pilot Quest right away too.

This game is so much more than a multi-game pack. UFO 50 has so much charm and creativity in each one of its 50 games making each of them extremely fun in their own right. There are MULTIPLE games included in UFO 50 that I would legitimately purchase on their own if that was the way they were sold. Beyond the fun in the games themselves there is a measure of creative genius in the way that the games are packaged as well. They are presented as if looking into another world where instead of then NES we got these 50 games and the little blurbs of history as well as the amount of tastfully re-used assets and characters and the perceived technological progression of the games throughout the chronology, are very well done. While each of the games on their own are quite simple, the games together are a very complex and impressive look into a universe of games never before seen. I've only finished a couple of the games and while some of them are extremely difficult I always find myself wanting to play more. This is a game I would recommend to anyone who likes games and especially to anyone who appreciates video game history.

First of all I want to say something about the music. I'm extremely impressed by the amount and variety and (something that probably only musicians will notice) how there's microtonality/experiments with tuning/intonation in a lot of the tracks. While still managing to keep super catchy and powerful melodies.
It's very innovative and fresh and I hope more video game composers do this.

The games are very polished. They feel like full games on their own. With most of them you can clearly tell what was their direct inspirations. But they all have some interesting twist, so they don't feel generic.

I'm very impressed with the amount of creativity and mastery of game design in this.
If it looks like it's something you would like, you definitely will.

50 games for $25?? What a steal!!!

For real though if you like retro games in any capacity you'll probably find at least 2-3 bangers in here for ya

This game captures the childhood magic of firing up random games you know almost nothing about and having a blast anyway. Not every game is going to be for you, but you will enjoy finding out for yourself which ones are the best in this "bundle" (and why it's Bushido Ball).

I've been very impressed with how each game feels like a vintage 80s game unshackled by the limitations of that era. Each game has some creative curveball that keeps it from being too predictable. Exploring this bundle is just fun, and hard to put down once you find your favorite games.
If you like arcade games, or retro style games, I cannot recommend this more. 10/10 no notes.

This game is just an exercise in how much frustration you can handle :
- No manual or tutorial explaining basic game mechanics
- No mini-maps in metroidvanias
- No (useful) maps for games that require careful planning to finish
- No continues or checkpoints. Games become so frustrating towards the end because if you want to practice lvl 40, you need to beat all the 39 previous ones anytime you die.

Even games in the 80s (which these are trying to emulate) had better QOL, they had manuals, NPCs with explanations or hints, magazines filled with tips and tricks and strategy guides with useful maps. The wikis for this game don't have much useful information eitherr, which makes me doubt many players even finish the games. It's a shame, because underneath the frustration are some great games with fantastic music. Hope they can patch this game with some basic QOL
Not only is there an incredible amount of content in this collection, each of the games also feel unique and original. Ufo50 is a dream for game explorers!
Love the variety of games. Easy to learn, fun to play. Love the simplistic layout of the games. Good levels of challenge to be found in most of these games. Great value.

A great time and if you skip every game by Derek Yu you'll have a better time than if you don't

TIP: You can see who made each game on Wikipedia :D

A wonderful mixture of weird and creative games, it's hard to, in reasonable space, do justice to UFO 50. And neither do I have to, content creators all around have milked this anthology of games like crazy. I'll simply join to the choir stating: it's good.

Its a compilation of a bunch of games and some of them individually have arguably been worth the price of the entire compilation.

I've beaten 6 games and completed the bonus objective on 4 of them so far, I've not touched over half the games still and I've had way more than enough fun to recommend this game.

From golf to simple arcade games to an entire puzzle platform game, this game has been a blast for the majority of the time I've put into it. It can be extremely challenging at times depending on the game you're playing, but there is something in here for everyone to enjoy... and if you enjoy a bit of every genre you're going to adore this game.

And that's not even going into some of the secrets you'll find if you have a keen eye ;)

i've been meaning to write this review hundreds of hours ago, but long story short: ufo 50 is one of the best values i've ever had in gaming.

each game is an interesting and deep experience. some games will vibe with you more than others, but in a game of 50 different games, i think that's impossible to avoid. the games run everything from platformers to rpg's, to modern game design like procedural generation and deckbuilding, all set in a surprisingly deep and interconnected alternate universe.

A truly unbelievable game. The amount of ideas on the table is staggering, and almost all its titles ooze originality. There are some obvious misses due to either mechanical failure or a desire to make the game feel "old" (looking at you, Combatants), but even if you were to only play the best 10 games in the collection, the price would be well worth it.

If you are at all partial to mechanically simple games, you will love UFO 50. It transcends its predecessors while maintaining a distinctly retro identity, and manages to subtly weave a charming meta-narrative in the process. It's a somewhat mind-boggling release in today's landscape, but it does not care. This one rules.

This is like the kinda game idea you have as a kid. "What if a game was just all of the the games" Most of the time you grow up and realize that's impossible. But some people don't give up on their childhood dreams and do the impossible. 50 games and all of them are good. I can't believe this. 10/10

would be cool if any of those 50 hip NES games were at least somewhat easy to get into and not ultra hard "classic difficulty"
I come home from work hating my own life and i wanna play a game, then i realize that i have to put actual effort and work if i wanna play any of these 50 games and it's like... bro.
but otherwise it's good if you're unemployed and work a dead-end job where you dont have to actively think and problem solve

You ever come across one of those suspiciously bootleg game cartridges, especially for the game boy series of handheld consoles, that had 25 or even 50 or more games on it? Too often they'd be repeats, or even poorly or even untranslated versions of games, but most of them were generally decent. UFO 50 brought those memories back, except this time there are no repeat games and, honestly, several of them are really fun so far. Cheers to Bug Hunter being a difficult but intriguing game and Paint Chase being a really fun reworking of Pac Man!

Yeah sure I've played about half an hour and I clearly have massive skill issues BUT this collection is really compelling. I'm glad to see a tribute to old arcades here on Steam, even though the alleged company behind them is actually just a couple of game developer *individuals*, and I hope we see more games like this. Maybe not the literal 50 odd arcade games part, but just a few new cool arcade games with catchy tunes, classic 8 bit visuals, and addictive gameplay would be great. People can have both 3D APRG experiences, roguelike card games, AND this arcade stuff amirite
A massive accomplishment with a commentary on game preservation and the dire state it's in. What a unique idea for a game.

This game is a major high watermark in indie game development, and a significant milestone in the art form. It's a slow burn to begin with, but it will get it's hooks into you if you give it time, and the marriage of old school fun with high level intentional artistry, is deeply compelling. It feels like the most classic Nintendo game, but goes above and beyond even that high bar. It is an anthology yes, but it is also clearly a deeply cohesive artistic vision. Out of 50 games, only 2 are lemons (Combatants, and Planet Zoldath). And stay away from Barbuta until you've got the bug. Start with Warptank if you need an in. Enjoy! Such a rare treat.

I have been abducted and brainwashed by UFO 50. I can't put this game down. 50 actually amazing games bundled in one package for $25. You might not like every game here, but if you can appreciate retro styled/inspired games I'd say you're guaranteed to find at least one you like. Or two. Or five.

A lot of these games could probably make it as independent titles with how big they are. But when they're all in one collection they elevate each other so much. You can easily jump out of one game and into another, and for me that seamlessness keeps things fresh and fun. I've completed a handful of games in my 43 hours of playtime so far, and I still have 12 whole games I haven't tried yet.

Not to mention the meta-narrative story and secrets woven across the collection. I've barely explored that side of UFO 50, but the fact that it's there is just another layer to what this game has to offer.

For the price and the variety of full and fantastic games, UFO 50 is truly a steal. I cannot recommend it enough.

Disappointed. Purchased because it reviewed so well, I guess on nostalgia... I grew up through the 80s and 90s playing games of that era. I tried every game here, all 50... and while there's a few that I threw a couple retries at, even those weren't really fun. And most were an immediate 'nope, back to library'. There's nothing here I'd ever want to play again, or feel any desire to complete. Regret the purchase and the time spent trying them all more. Wish I could refund. 16 hours may seem like I enjoyed myself, but it is only about 20 min per title.

No matter what you played on the NES, this game is guaranteed to hit you with nostalgia for that system, from the graphics, to the sounds, to the gameplay. There's enough modern game design philosophy to help the games less frustrating than some you may have played back in the day, but the games are still made just a bit jank/stuff to still invoke that old school feel. With 50 different games on offer, no one will love all of them, but I have loved quite a lot more than I even expected I would.
most games have much more depth than you realize, incredibly charming and genuinely fun despite not being huge on retro games, also an insane amount of content for completionists.
Remember those X-in-1 games you had as a kid? This is like that except the games are all good actually

These are 50 retro styled games of varying lengths and genres, all made for a fictional console called the LX in the 80s. The games are linked through easter eggs, game design practices, developers, and even sequels to further lean into this narrative (and yes, there is an optional ARG). 

Some games are 30 minutes long, some are 20 hours. Regardless of the length, each game feels like a complete experience that is fun, polished, creative, and excellently designed. There are tons of extra layers of depth in each and every game, so you can put as much time into game as you want, 100%ing the game, mastering it, or just going for a high score. 10/10, you will find at least one game here that you love.

It’s as if I went on vacation to a parallel universe and was able to enjoy fresh takes on genre-defining games at will. Priced at $25, the value of this title is astonishing, offering something for nearly everyone to enjoy. I find myself picking titles at random and getting easily lost in them, no matter the genre I'm exploring. Even the antiquated mechanics of Barbuta, with its hardcore, saveless nature, propelled me to complete the game, all while enjoying every bit of early 80's frustration that accompanied each discovery. This is some of the purest game design to be found in 2024 and is honestly a breath of fresh air (even if that air is tinged with nostalgia from a distance.) UFO 50 is a necessary library addition for just about every gamer out there.

Edit (9/26):
It's like smoking some kind of tolerance-defying cannabis sativa with an infinite burn. I haven't popped my cherry in Rock On! Island yet but after beating it I'm happy to report that the action theme has etched it's way into my dreams and daily routine. I'm considering leaving the game open while I slave away at work just to relive the satisfaction from completing that cart. I ain't coughing this smoke up anytime soon.

The exact definition of all killer, no filler. I don't mean I love all 50 but it's impossible not to be taken aback by how utterly deliberate and realized every single one of them is. Every game has its audience and I think every person on the planet given the chance could find a game for them in here. An absolutely literal must-buy.
Top recommendations: Magic Garden, Campanella 2, Party House, Pingolf

9 minutes in, I love it already!
Update: Do I hear microtonal tuning in the OST? Wow!
Update 2: Now I wish this video game platform actually physically existed :-)
Update 3: Spending way too much time on Party House :-)
DAWG! MINI AND MAX IS WORTH $25 BY ITSELF. THIS IS A FUCKING OPEN WORLD GAME MADE IN THE STYLE OF OLD NES GAMES. I LOVE IT

I am honestly in awe that this even exists. It's like showing up to a dinner party and getting fed with incredible delicious food, and then finding out that this was just the appetizer and there are 6 more courses coming. I am almost overwhelmed at the sheer amount of quality, gripping content in this collection of games. Not all are my exact genre but god damn the ones that are, are SO DANG GOOD. I'm sitting here laughing my ass off opening up game after game and just seeing how much depth exists in each one. This is something to chew on and digest for ages. Really epic. Super glad I decided to try it out after hearing so much about it. WIll be playing this for a long long time.

The amount of variety in this collection along with the quality of each game is astounding. At the present time I've experienced maybe a little over a fifth of the games and have already found some that are genuine favorite time wasters. It almost feels criminal that this game is only $25.

The games ive played of this collection are really good pick up and play experiences. You may not like all of them but the ones you do will feel like picking up an old console games as a kid. This collection is so deceptive because while it looks kinda cheap, the games in this collection are brimming with mechanics that could define an entire other game experience.

I've been continually surprised by the depth of the games in this collection. It's not just a collection of ideas, the ideas of often executed well and placed in extremely fun, cool video games. While there've been a few times where I've wished that a concept had just a little bit more depth to it (I finished Pilot Quest and could really go for a full-blown sequel, for example), it's just a great, clever collection. Very neat secret(s), too!
Reminds me a lot of the old plug n' play systems but actually good. Now all we need is an indie Patrick Maze Game.

It's good.
50 games, just like when you found your dad's nes in the back of the garage as a kid and played through the whole collection, no context just vibes, figuring out how each game worked and swapping cartridges on a whim.

Every game I've played so far is good (25~/50) and they are all fully fledged games that feel like they genuinely could have been individual products back in the era the collection is calling back to.

Also it's wonderful to finally buy something that says '50 games inside!' and they're actually real, good games, it's not a scam, there's no filler, it's great. Play Forever!

I feel pretty mixed on UFO 50. Like, I can tell that a lot of the games in the collection are objectively good, but I enjoyed almost none of them. I sampled all the games on offer, with a bit more playtime on the ones I was enjoying, but only ended up with 7 I actually wanted to continue playing at all. Now, this is not a knock on the game, I've just found as I get older that I don't really enjoy difficult games or arcade-y games very much, and those cover a lot of the games in the collection. Unfortunately, by the time I got through trying all the games, I went and looked back at the ones I had marked as favorites and didn't really feel the desire to return to any of them.

I am still going to recommend the game, but with caveats. If your tastes are similar to mine, you should probably give the game a miss. If you really like early 8-bit games, with the clunkiness and difficulty that entails, and if you like arcade-style games, you'll probably have a really good time here. For me, my retro tastes tend more towards 4th (SNES/Genesis/TG16) to the 6th (PS2/Gamecube/Xbox/Dreamcast). I like some 8-bit classics, but I prefer the next few gens after it.

TL;DR, UFO 50 is good, but I didn't really like it. If your tastes are different, you'll probably like it though.

Reminds me of going to a local video rental store, grabbing an NES game, and playing whatever it was for a weekend. Back then we kinda knew what we were getting, but a lot of times it was trash.

This is like that but boiled down so that all the games are at least a C+ in terms of quality and you can get to enjoy the uncanny nostalgia.

I don't know where the devs could go after this. To my taste as an old man, this is peak.
I hope they make a direct sequel that's just more games, maybe even a Super UFO 50 and have the theme be a SNES era system.
There's a bunch of good games here, I love House Party, Valgard, Waldorf's Journey and Bushido Ball the most.

One of the best games I've ever bought!
The amount of quality games you get for only $25 is insane!
Every PC gamer should own this.
This game rules! Easily one of my favorite games ever. . . multiple of my favorite games ever :)

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (95%): players love the variety of the games and the gameplay.
Complaints are few and spread across different topics.

details.text: Recent reviews are about as positive as the all-time score, at 97%, so the mood has held steady.
Players who have just started are less won over, at 70% positive, while long-time players reach 99%.
